claims.implementation: backend/arkali/control/architecture/gates/provider_source.py - the source-level half of the canonical `shadow_registry` gate. ProviderVocabulary derives the provider token from the owner context's final segment, the owned concerns from `fields_owned`, and the forbidden operations from the map's own `<operation>_permitted: false` keys, expanded morphologically; no consumer, concern or context is named in the module, asserted against its own AST. ConsumerScan walks every module under each declared consumer's declared module root and refuses, by AST binding construct rather than by text: a class field, attribute, module-level name, function or defaulted parameter whose tokens carry the provider token AND every token of an owned concern; the same shape reached through a Field(alias=...), a dict key or an identifier-shaped keyword string; a bare concern declared inside a provider-shaped class; a provider-qualified name carrying a forbidden operation; and a provider-shaped value assigned to a self attribute. backend/arkali/control/architecture/gates/authority_gates.py - ShadowRegistryGate composes the retained declaration half with the new source half under one gate id, because AUTHORITY_MAP.yaml declares the gate set. Discovery is by walk at call time, so a module added to a consumer tomorrow is scanned; a consumer with no module on disk, and a run that scanned nothing, are violations rather than a quiet pass.
